subject.title: cron: ghost runs recorded as ok when gateway is down (durationMs < 50ms)

question: Should OpenClaw accept the linked PR's defaulted, persisted, configurable ghost-run warning surface for fast main-session `next-heartbeat` cron handoffs, or require a narrower diagnostic shape?
rationale: The bug is source-reproducible, but the proposed solution crosses config, protocol/run-log, docs, and UI surfaces, which AGENTS.md treats as compatibility-sensitive and product-direction-sensitive.

options.title: Refresh and decide the linked PR
options.body: Keep this issue open while https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/72677 is refreshed, conflict-resolved, re-proven on exact head, and reviewed for the accepted warning/config/protocol shape.

options.title: Request a narrower diagnostic
options.body: Ask for a smaller warning or run-log-only implementation if maintainers do not want a new defaulted cron config key or generated protocol field.

options.title: Choose a different semantic fix
options.body: Pause the warning approach if maintainers want cron to fail, skip, or await processing instead of recording `ok` with a diagnostic warning.

recommendation.title: Refresh and decide the linked PR
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/72677 is refreshed, conflict-resolved, re-proven on exact head, and reviewed for the accepted warning/config/protocol shape.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest current-history owner for the central cron dispatch and gateway run-log paths involved in this decision.
